newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees no major change to auto import rules.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees no major change to auto import rules.

text.p: Brazil's consultations at World Trade Organization (WTO) next week over its tariffs on imported cars will not result in a major policy change, a Brazilian trade official said on Friday.

As a first step in the WTO dispute resolution process, the European Union last month requested the consultations over the tariff system, which offers a special 35 percent tariff on imports from carmakers with a manufacturing base in Brazil. Other manufacturers must pay 65 percent on their imports.
"There is nothing hostile about the consultations," said Jose Alfredo Graca Lima, the head of the Foreign Ministry's Economics Department.
He said similar consultations with the United States and Japan had not led to any steps being taken toward the formation of a panel, the final stage of the dispute process.

The Brazilian officials were due to meet with their EU counterparts in Geneva June 9 and 10. They would then travel to London for an informal meeting with representatives of the Japanese government June 12 and 13, Graca Lima said.
Brazil introduced the tariff system last year amid concern over its widening trade deficit and in a bid to stimulate foreign investment.

In a concession, carmakers from the EU, Japan and South Korea were allowed to export a total of 50,000 cars a year to Brazil at the 35 percent tariff rate under a quota system due to expire August 20.

Graca Lima said the meetings in Geneva and London would help Brazil decide whether to renew the quotas after that date. He declined to say whether there would be any change in the number of cars allowed under the system.
"The quota system could undergo some kind of modification, perhaps a redistribution, but there will not necessarily be a reduction in the number," he said.
Under the current quota system, Japanese carmakers are entitled to export 47.5 percent of the total 50,000 low-tariff cars entering Brazil, South Korea 31.1 percent and the EU 19.4 percent.
